iñjati: iñjati [Vedic ṛñjati (cp. P. ajjati). Also found as ingati (so Veda), and as ang in Sk. anga = P. añja & ingha & Vedic pali--angati to turn about. See also ānejja & añjati1] to shake, move, turn about, stir D I.56; S I.107, 132, 181 (aniñjamāna ppr. med. "impassive"); III.211; Th 1, 42; 2, 231; Nd2 s. v. (+ calati vedhati); Vism 377; DA I.167. -- pp. iñjita (q. v.).
iñjanā: iñjanā (f.) & °aṃ (nt.) [fr. iñj, see iñjati] shaking, movement, motion Sn 193 (= calanā phandanā SnA 245); Nett 88 (= phandanā C.). an° immobility, steadfastness Ps I.15; II.118.
iñjita: iñjita [pp. of iñjati] shaken, moved Th 1, 386 (an°). Usually as nt. iñjitaṃ shaking, turning about, movement, vacillation M I.454; S I.109; IV.202; A II.45; Sn 750, 1040 (pl. iñjitā), 1048 (see Nd2 140); Dh 255; Vbh 390. <-> On the 7 iñjitas see J.P. T.S. 1884, 58.
iñjitatta: iñjitatta (nt.) [abstr. fr. iñjita nt.] state of vacillation, wavering, motion S V.315 (kāyassa).
